overview.title: A Waterford base for making the packaging Ireland, the UK and Europe already need.
overview.subtitle: The first phase makes printed paper packaging: pizza boxes in different specifications and sizes, plus takeaway products made from the same paper-and-board materials.
overview.description: The campus is planned as a local production, storage and dispatch hub serving Ireland, the United Kingdom and wider European Union markets. A later phase can add pharmaceutical packaging, but only with the higher standards, controlled processes, plastics and aluminium capabilities that regulated products require.

highlights.label: Pizza boxes
highlights.desc: Multiple box formats with printing, conversion, hygiene control, storage and dispatch.

highlights.label: Takeaway products
highlights.desc: Paper-based takeaway packaging using compatible material handling, printing and finishing capability.

highlights.label: Future pharma phase
highlights.desc: A separately assessed expansion using higher-specification quality systems and plastics/aluminium printing and conversion.

overview.note: Scope boundary: this is packaging-material manufacturing — not food production and not pharmaceutical production. Food-related packaging requires hygiene controls; pharma is a future regulated phase, subject to validation.

opportunity.title: Start with familiar paper products, then serve Ireland, the UK and the wider EU.
opportunity.intro: The source model points to a large, recurring demand base. The figures below are market references and planning inputs — not guaranteed sales.

metrics.label: ROI + NI boxes / year · source model
Additional addressable markets beyond Ireland and UK

cards.title: Different pizza-box specifications
cards.body: 10-inch individual, 12-inch standard and 16-inch family/party formats are shown in the source model, with different demand and die-cutting requirements.

cards.title: Print where demand happens
cards.body: Customer graphics, branding and product information can be printed and converted locally for Ireland, the UK and selected EU customers.

cards.title: A disciplined expansion path
cards.body: Paper pizza and takeaway lines come first. Pharma packaging follows only after separate regulatory, quality, materials and facility design work.

opportunity.callout: The opportunity is not limited to Ireland and the UK: the campus can develop an EU-facing customer and logistics strategy, subject to market, certification, language, freight and customer validation.

process.title: From paper roll to hygienically controlled, printed and dispatched packaging.
process.intro: Pizza boxes and takeaway products are food-related packaging materials. The operating model therefore includes cleaning, sanitation and hygiene-control activities alongside printing and conversion.

steps.title: Receive
steps.body: Paper, board, inks and approved materials arrive and are checked.

steps.title: Print
steps.body: Brand graphics and product information are applied.

steps.title: Convert
steps.body: Creasing, die-cutting, folding and forming create the required format.

steps.title: Sanitise
steps.body: Production areas, relevant equipment and contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitised under hygiene procedures.

steps.title: Check
steps.body: Dimensions, print, structure, hygiene records and pack-out are inspected.

steps.title: Store + dispatch
steps.body: Finished goods move to protected storage and regional delivery.

cards.title: Food-packaging hygiene
cards.body: The facility will require documented cleaning and sanitation routines, hygienic zoning, staff hygiene procedures, suitable chemicals and records appropriate to food-contact packaging requirements.

cards.title: Flexible production logic
cards.body: A common paper-and-board platform can support multiple box sizes and takeaway formats, subject to machine configuration, tooling and throughput validation.

cards.title: Planning before commitment
cards.body: Equipment, layout, raw-material volumes, staffing and shift assumptions must be verified with suppliers and engineering partners before any capacity number becomes a commitment.

campus.title: Plan the whole operating system — factory, hygiene, logistics and people.
campus.intro: The current planning basis is approximately 1.6 acres. The layout must fit production, inventory, hygiene controls, people and vehicle movement safely, with room for a credible next phase.
right: Accommodation / dormitory provision for build and equipment teams
Reserved separation for future pharma work
Expansion and compliance review before regulated production
campus.note: Construction option: assess rapid-build industrial techniques from China alongside conventional local construction. The preferred solution must satisfy Irish and EU planning, building, fire, workplace, hygiene and environmental requirements.

delivery.title: Make locally, source intelligently, deliver faster across Ireland, the UK and Europe.
delivery.intro: The source model compares importing finished boxes with bringing dense raw rolls to Waterford for local conversion. The figures are indicative model outputs and require freight, material and customer validation.

metrics.label: Illustrative containers: finished boxes vs raw rolls

phases.title: 1 · Validate
phases.body: Confirm customers, product specifications, materials, equipment, hygiene requirements and the 1.6-acre layout.

phases.title: 2 · Design
phases.body: Compare local construction with rapid-build options from China; complete Irish and EU-facing planning, engineering and logistics design.

phases.title: 3 · Install
phases.body: Procure, install, commission and train operators, hygiene, quality, maintenance and warehouse teams.

phases.title: 4 · Scale
phases.body: Ramp pizza and takeaway packaging for Ireland, the UK and EU markets, then assess a separately controlled pharma phase.

cards.title: Three-market delivery strategy
cards.body: The campus is intended to serve Ireland, the United Kingdom and wider EU customers. Delivery times and routes will depend on customer location, carrier contracts, customs requirements and product certification.

delivery.imageAlt: Illustration of local paper-roll conversion and regional packaging logistics

employment.title: A manufacturing project that creates value beyond the factory gate.
employment.intro: The employment number should be set after equipment, throughput and shift design are confirmed. The public case can still be made clearly today: local production, local logistics, local management, hygiene capability and future technical skills.

metrics.label: Year-3 gross revenue in source model
Year-3 EBITDA in source model · indicative

employment.jobsBody: The project creates roles across machine operation, print and conversion, hygiene and sanitation, quality, maintenance, warehousing, transport coordination, engineering, administration and management. Final headcount is deliberately left open until the operating case is engineered.
support: New local manufacturing and technical jobs
Taxable trading activity and local supplier spend
Lower dependence on imported finished boxes
A platform for future regulated packaging capability
employment.taxNote: Illustrative source-model reference: €24.6M Year-3 revenue and €8.17M EBITDA. At Ireland's 12.5% corporation-tax rate, 12.5% of EBITDA would be approximately €1.02M before depreciation, financing, allowances and other tax adjustments — not a tax forecast.
employment.callout: Government support requested: planning and site coordination, IDA / local-authority engagement, grant and investment pathways, training connections and cross-agency facilitation.

close.title: A practical route from concept to a validated Waterford project.
close.quote: We are asking for the coordination needed to validate and deliver a real local packaging manufacturing base — starting with paper products for Ireland, the UK and Europe, and building responsibly toward regulated packaging.

nextSteps.title: Confirm the operating case
nextSteps.body: Agree customer demand, product formats, equipment, raw materials, hygiene controls, freight assumptions and the defensible employment model.

nextSteps.title: Confirm the site plan
nextSteps.body: Test the 1.6-acre layout for production, two warehouses, sanitation, logistics, offices, accommodation and future separation.

nextSteps.title: Open the public pathway
nextSteps.body: Coordinate planning, IDA, grants, training, construction and investment discussions.

close.leftBody: Technical review, supplier quotations, CE and hygiene checks, preliminary layout, raw-material tenders and customer validation.
close.rightBody: Support a coordinated route to confirm the site, validate the model and unlock the next stage of investment and employment planning.
